blocks.text: Wesgro is accountable for twelve initiatives and does part of the work in all eighteen; for the other six, the accountable lead sits with another tier, and the plan names it.

The matrix below assigns each initiative to the four roles: responsible (R) for doing the work, accountable (A) for the result, consulted (C) before decisions and informed (I) of progress. Where Wesgro is accountable and does the work itself, the cell reads A/R. Assignments are proposals for Steerco to confirm, built from the actions in Chapter 3.

blocks.message: Wesgro is accountable for twelve initiatives; provincial departments, municipalities or site operators are accountable for six, and SOEs or national departments do part of the work in four.

blocks.text: National government and the state-owned entities

Four levers sit outside the province and cannot be bought or marketed into place. Route rights and visas sit with the national tier (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p58), the airport and port capital programmes with national SOEs (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p103, p112) and policing with SAPS. The plan treats them as an escalation agenda (I17), carried by Steerco through DEDAT to the national departments and SOEs. Wesgro's Advocacy and Advisory unit, set up to build evidence-based policy feedback on levers the province does not control, is proposed to run it day to day (Wesgro, Strategic Plan 2025/26 to 2029/30, p27). DEDAT's visa study supplies its visa asks, already ranked (BDO for DEDAT, Western Cape Visa Regime Study, Jul 2024, p34). Each item is stated as a decision, an owner and a date the province is asking for. Wesgro's own route work (I6) runs inside the existing agreements meanwhile.

DEDAT is a standing member of Steerco and the accountable lead where the lever is policy or funding rather than promotion: quality standards (I10), LTO funding and climate risk (I13) and the labour analysis (I18). The Department of Mobility leads the transport half of corridor mobility (I8), including the airport leg with the City and ACSA. It also joins the levy case (I14) and brings its Integrated Transport Hub into the data protocol (I16). The Provincial Treasury's district reviews feed the data protocol and the IDP step (I13, I16). Wesgro's units lead the demand, access, product and data initiatives and report through the programme office.

Municipalities and LTOs hold the assets, the selling bodies and the visitor services that the regional and inclusion initiatives depend on. They lead the community selling bodies in the pilots (I12), attach covenants to public assets (I12, I14) and carry the route and product work in their districts (I3, I9). The City of Cape Town is a partner on segments, events, routes, cruise, mobility, product, flagship sites, community pilots and safety (I1, I2, I6 to I9, I11, I12, I17). Cape Town Tourism is a partner on segments, routes and data (I1, I6, I16), and both sit on Steerco. The City's framework for 2019 to 2024 proposed three plans the initiatives can build on where they run. They are an air, rail and cruise access programme, a Cape Town+ offer and a Tourist Safety Programme (City of Cape Town, Tourism Development Framework 2019 to 2024, p5, p6).
The private sector and site operators

Airlines decide frequency and gauge, hotel investors decide the mid-scale tier and attraction operators manage their own capacity. The plan gives them the evidence and the demand case. It asks for the decisions it cannot make for them: seats on full routes (I6), investment in secondary nodes (I14) and visitor-flow management at flagship sites, where the operators are accountable (I11).
